exact_diagnostics.status: DONE — twelve exact elementary source-interface diagnostic families

families.name: Probability mean versus determinant total
families.argument: In an arbitrary common basis all three logarithmic ratios are 2. The probability mean is 2; the determinant total is 6. The displayed equality in Theorem 1.15 needs division by rank, while the signed mean convention is retained throughout. Rank zero requires a separate convention.

families.name: Joint-coordinate spectral pushforward
families.argument: The definition of successive minima fixes the sign. The joint negative-log coordinate pushforward must be x-y.

families.name: Positive power and signed-volume scaling
families.argument: The source writes vol(F)=vol(F,trivial)=-mean log F. Direct scalar computation gives log(G^s/F^t)=t vol(F)-s vol(G). Both occurrences of s-t must be t-s.

families.name: The power in the degree-normalized p metric
families.argument: Scalar graded norms exp(2m) times the reference have all normalized slopes 2. The pth moment is 2^p, while the unsquared normalized distance is 2. The last term of the displayed d_p^p chain needs the pth power.

families.name: Positive ray-limit estimate and missing second direction
families.argument: The time-zero norm contributes eta_0(v)^(1/t), tending to 1. Comparing to eta_s(v) without dividing its logarithm by s and then accounting for the initial value gives the false displayed lower bound. The scalar rays also detect the repeated unprimed limiting direction in Theorem 1.51.

families.name: The literal graded bound does not restrict the class

facts.literal_witness: choose the comparison graded norm to be zeta itself

families.argument: The comparison norm is unrestricted in the printed definition, so choosing the norm itself makes C=0 for every graded norm. The candidate is submultiplicative because (m+n)^2>=m^2+n^2 and Gauss products are bounded by the product norms. Its normalized relative laws escape to infinity. A fixed admissible degree-one/model reference, or an independently defined bounded class, is necessary before the compact-law theorem can be used. This does not refute the theorem for genuinely linearly bounded norms.

families.name: Increasing bounded graded norms need not converge strongly
families.argument: min(m+n,k)<=min(m,k)+min(n,k) proves submultiplicativity. The family increases and converges at each fixed degree. The strong distance to its supremum is sup_{m>=1}(m-min(m,k))/m=1, since these numbers are at most 1 and tend to 1 as m tends to infinity. This disproves the general inference from monotone boundedness to strong convergence. It is not a counterexample to the special chord family in Proposition 2.12 or to that intended conclusion.

families.name: Stop-loss scalar shift before taking a power
families.argument: Write tF=F^t and A for the norm action. Then exp(tc times degree) A(tF,eta)=A(t(exp(c times degree)F),eta). Putting tc inside the direction before applying the power t instead gives t squared c. With corrected shifts and the volume-of-maximum input, the cocycle calculation is a conditional route to the stop-loss limit.

families.name: The finite spectral evaluation domain exceeds the limiting support

facts.space: P1 over a trivially valued ground field

families.argument: The norm is submultiplicative: in the constant coefficient the product bound uses exp(m+n)=exp(m)exp(n); the remaining coefficients have weight one and are bounded by the input norms. It has a common genuine linear bound. Its normalized constant-monomial slope is -1 in every degree, but its limiting spectral support is {0}. A function supplied only on S cannot be evaluated there. Specify a common full interval, a global convex extension or a precise quotient convention before using the literal functional-calculus formula.

families.name: Flat apex, constant function, dimension and convexity
families.argument: The displayed weights compute the apex and scalar constants directly. When S is a singleton the proposed cone is one dimensional, so an infinite-dimensional conclusion needs nondegenerate spectral support. The L1 norm is not strictly convex: two distinct unit vectors have a unit midpoint. A broader metric-flat definition can still be used, but it differs from the introduction’s strict-convexity requirement. Theorem 2.13 proves norm membership only under a bounded right-derivative premise, which needs reconciliation with the stated whole function class.

families.name: Finite action comparisons and explicit finite-p versus infinity boundary

facts.action: largest genuine norm dominated by eta(v)F(v)
facts.direct_comparison: exp(-C-D) eta F <= eta prime F prime <= exp(C+D) eta F

families.argument: The norm envelope is monotone and commutes with positive scalar multiplication. Applying it to the product-gauge comparisons proves the finite infinity contraction directly, without a spherical-completeness hypothesis. Determinant factorization and the calibrated maximum/volume identity give the cited finite d1 contraction. The rare-monomial family illustrates that finite-p asymptotic equivalence is strictly weaker than strong infinity equivalence; no rank-dependent finite-dimensional equivalence constant may be used uniformly in the section degree.
